property_summary: Only the current owner can change the owner; the mutant allows any caller to change the owner.
After any successful transferOwnership call by a non-owner, the correct contract keeps owner unchanged, while the mutant updates owner.
After a successful transferOwnership call by the owner, the state variable owner must equal the newOwner argument; the bug sets owner to address(0) instead.

After transferOwnership is called by the current owner with any address argument, the owner state variable must equal the argument address; the buggy version leaves owner unchanged, violating this rule for any newOwner != current owner.

For any caller, a call to owned() must always revert unless the caller is the owner. The buggy version removes this restriction, allowing any address to call owned() without reverting, which violates the invariant that owned() is only callable by the owner.
owned() must always revert when called by a non-owner; the bug makes it always succeed, so the revert flag differs for any non-owner caller.
For any non-owner caller, a call to owned() must revert; the bug lets the call succeed, changing the revert flag.
Any caller different from the owner MUST revert when calling transferOwnership; the buggy version allows any caller to succeed.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner must either remain unchanged or change to the new owner, but the bug allows an unauthorized caller to set the owner, violating this invariant.
The owner state variable must remain unchanged when a non-owner calls transferOwnership, but the bug allows any sender to change it.

After a successful call to transferOwnership, the previous owner must differ from the new owner; the bug makes the require condition always true, allowing a non-owner to set owner to itself, violating this post-condition.
For any non-owner caller, a call to transferOwnership must revert; the bug makes the require true for all callers, so a non-owner can change owner without revert.

After transferOwnership, the owner of the contract is the new owner for the correct version, but for the buggy version when called by anyone other than the current owner, the owner remains the caller instead of changing to the new owner.

After a successful call to transferOwnership(newOwner) by the current owner, the contract owner must equal newOwner; the bug sets owner to msg.sender instead, so it fails for any call where newOwner != msg.sender.

After the current owner delegates ownership transfer to any newOwner address via transferOwnership, the contract's owner MUST equal newOwner; the bug illegally assigns owner to msg.sender (the current owner) instead, so the rule fails whenever the current owner is not the intended newOwner.
After any successful transferOwnership call, the owner must equal the newOwner address passed; the bug leaves owner unchanged so fails for any address different from the current owner.
